subject: Report results from latent Moderation (probe with wald test)

messages.author: dc83f318e1e834c9
messages.subject: Report results from latent Moderation (probe with wald test)
parts:
Hi,

I want to publish the results of my latent interaction, which I specified using the indProd-package and probed with the probe2wayMC-function of the semTools-package. No I was wondering whether I only report the significant result of the SEM (beta, p-value) or also the results of the Wald-test (probe2WayMC). And if I report both, could anybody recommend an approach to test the slopes of the interaction with the wald test unarbitrarily? with a latent variable, it's tricky to justify the concrete values I use to probe the interaction, I recon? Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Report results from latent Moderation (probe with wald test)
parts: I was wondering whether I only report the significant result of the SEM (beta, p-value) or also the results of the Wald-test (probe2WayMC).

Not sure what your field is, but APA style recommends reporting the parameter along with a measure of uncertainty (SE or CI), its NHST statistic with p value, and a standardized measure of effect size (e.g., the standardized slope in the std.all column).

And if I report both, could anybody recommend an approach to test the slopes of the interaction with the wald test unarbitrarily? with a latent variable, it's tricky to justify the concrete values I use to probe the interaction, I recon?

It is up to you to decide what values of the moderator are not arbitrary.  The default is the M +/- SD because that is a common convention and captures a good representation of the distribution of the moderator if it is normally distributed.

FYI, don't trust your results yet.  There is a bug in the probe2Way*() functions that causes the estimates and/or SEs to be switched between focal predictor and moderator, depending on the order of variable names specified.  I won't be able to fix the bug until after my teaching wraps up for the semester.  Once I do, I will push a new semTools to CRAN, so you will know the bug is fixed when you can update the package to 0.5-4.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
